solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Showy performances that may be right in front of your eyes (10)

annotation.definition2: that may be right in front of your eyes

blocks.clueFragment: that may be right in front of your eyes
blocks.note: glasses, worn just in front of the eyes

annotation.surface: Something so dazzling on stage that it fills your whole view.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half reads like more praise for the show, but it is a playful description of a pair of glasses.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are plain dictionary ones: lavish shows, and the glasses that sit on your nose just before your eyes.

entries.clue: Piece of wisdom is a gem (5)

blocks.note: a precious saying, from a common idiom about wisdom

annotation.surface: A wise saying praised as a real gem.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase 'pearls of wisdom' links the two senses.
annotation.definitionFit: A jewel from an oyster, and by the idiom 'pearls of wisdom' a wise saying, so both senses hold.

entries.clue: Charlie, very old at home, unable to get out (5,2)

blocks.note: being in means being at home

annotation.surface: An elderly man called Charlie, housebound.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one old man stuck indoors; in fact each phrase supplies a separate chunk.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain phrase for trapped: shut in as if behind bars, with no way out.

annotation.surface: A foot placed behind the other.
annotation.walkthrough: FT is the standard abbreviation for foot as a measurement.
annotation.definitionFit: A nautical term for the back part of a ship, so a plain synonym for towards the rear.

entries.clue: Personal servant’s dismal day, running around (5,4)

annotation.surface: A servant having a gloomy day, rushed off their feet.
annotation.walkthrough: The servant's busy day is the whole anagram, with 'running around' telling you to rearrange it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by role: the woman who attended a lady personally, dressing her and keeping her clothes.

blocks.note: a wipe is a disposable tissue

annotation.surface: Nicking a little tissue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pinch' looks like a verb about fingers but means steal.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for stealing, so a plain slang synonym.

entries.clue: Require half lens for one with small eye (6)

blocks.note: first two of the four letters of LENS

annotation.surface: Someone with a small eye needing half a lens.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a person with poor sight; the eye is the hole a thread goes through.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the sewing tool has a tiny hole, its eye, for the thread.

annotation.surface: A sailor trying to earn a good grade.
annotation.walkthrough: TAR for sailor is a crossword staple.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the thing you aim at is your mark.

blocks.note: a golf club for long shots

annotation.surface: A motoring organisation such as the AA.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s reads as possessive but stands for 'is', joining two definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: Two plain senses: someone at the wheel of a car, and the golf club used for long tee shots.

indicatorNotes.losing: the PM loses the letters named next

annotation.surface: A Prime Minister cheerful at having lost weight.
annotation.walkthrough: Stone reads as a weight lost (a stone is 14 pounds); it is literally the STONE at the end of a 19th-century British PM's name.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for pleased or delighted.

indicatorNotes.about: the girl goes around the role

blocks.note: the top part in a play

annotation.surface: An actress lying her way into the starring part.
annotation.walkthrough: The girl is split open so the role sits inside her.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to lead someone astray by false impressions.

entries.clue: Staffs playing area in Notts town (9)

annotation.surface: Staff at a sports ground in a Nottinghamshire town.
annotation.walkthrough: Staffs looks like Staffordshire, a neighbouring county, but is the verb; Notts is Nottinghamshire, an English county.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a market town in Nottinghamshire, abbreviated Notts.

blocks.note: a billiards stroke where the cue ball hits two others

annotation.surface: A billiards player shot with a gun.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot by' suggests a shooting victim, but the shot is a stroke the player makes.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the old heavy artillery piece, and a billiards stroke hitting both object balls.

blocks.note: to aver is to maintain or declare

annotation.surface: Someone keeping their energy up by picking fights.
annotation.walkthrough: Maintains means asserts here, not keeps up.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: being opposed or hostile to something.

entries.clue: Not all crews naturally returning solution (6)

indicatorNotes.Not all: only part of the words is used
indicatorNotes.returning: the letters come back the other way

annotation.surface: Rowing crews coming back with the obvious fix.
annotation.walkthrough: The run spans the two words, then reads backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what solves a question or puzzle.

entries.clue: Japanese fighter, one with a curious case of arms raised (7)

indicatorNotes.case of: the case is the outside of ARMS
indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, raised means read upwards

annotation.surface: A warrior with an odd weapons case, hands up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Case of arms' suggests a weapons box but means the outer letters of ARMS; the whole string I-A-RUM-AS is read upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the hereditary warrior class of feudal Japan.

indicatorNotes.brewing: the letters are stirred up like a brew

annotation.surface: A bad batch of home brew poured away.
annotation.walkthrough: Duff is British slang for useless, which suits both the beer and its letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: turned away or snubbed, typically an offer or advance.

indicatorNotes.lead extracted from: the first letter is taken off

blocks.note: the Humber estuary in north-east England

annotation.surface: Brown mud and lead pollution pulled from a river mouth.
annotation.walkthrough: Lead reads as the metal but means the first letter; the estuary loses its H.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a natural brown earth pigment, whose name serves as the colour adjective.

entries.clue: Be depressed by exercise after very short time (4)

indicatorNotes.after: the exercise goes after the time

annotation.surface: Feeling low after only a brief workout.
annotation.walkthrough: MO, as in 'half a mo', is British for a moment.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to sulk around listlessly, feeling low.

indicatorNotes.carrying: the phrase holds the answer inside it

annotation.surface: A poker-faced mobster packing a big blade.
annotation.walkthrough: The word is an East African one, so the crossing letters and the run across the two words do the work.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an East African machete with a broad heavy blade.

annotation.surface: A black uniform suitable for the office.
annotation.walkthrough: Uniform looks like clothing but is the letter U.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: in working order and able to be used.

entries.clue: Shaving match involving two people, we hear (6)

indicatorNotes.we hear: what we hear is a sound, not a spelling

annotation.surface: A shaving contest between two rivals.
annotation.walkthrough: Shaving means a thin slice cut off, not a razor.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a thin strip cut off, as from an apple or a fingernail.

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up means read upwards

blocks.note: the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

annotation.surface: An Irish gathering keen for pudding.
annotation.walkthrough: Party reads as a celebration; the DUP is a Northern Irish political party.
annotation.definitionFit: A British informal word for pudding, the sweet course, so a regional synonym.

entries.clue: Excited lad married fluttery little thing (3,7)

annotation.surface: A newlywed young man in a flutter.
annotation.walkthrough: Fluttery reads as the groom's nerves; it describes a butterfly.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a common butterfly, fluttery and small.
